claims.text: A calibrated Hubbard U term within non-collinear DFT including spin-orbit coupling will correctly predict ferromagnetic ground states in transition-metal systems.
The proposed DFT method captures the exchange splitting necessary for ferromagnetism.
The proposed DFT method captures subtle spin-polarization effects relevant to ferromagnetic ordering.
The target material is a transition-metal compound or alloy with potentially competing magnetic interactions.
Ground-state determination should be performed at 0 K or in the low-temperature limit.
The intervention is to replace non-spin-polarized or collinear DFT without Hubbard U and spin-orbit coupling with calibrated DFT+U including non-collinearity and spin-orbit coupling.
Subtle energy differences among magnetic states must be accurately resolved to identify the ground state.
Exchange splitting and spin polarization are the electronic-structure mediators of the predicted magnetic state.
Standard DFT underestimates on-site electron-electron interactions, and the Hubbard U term corrects this underestimation.
Non-collinear DFT and spin-orbit coupling account for anisotropic magnetic interactions.
Combining Hubbard U, non-collinearity, and spin-orbit coupling provides an accurate energy balance that stabilizes the ferromagnetic configuration.
The predicted ferromagnetic state will have a lower total energy than alternative magnetic configurations.
The predicted state will have non-zero magnetic moments consistent with ferromagnetic ordering.
Standard non-spin-polarized or collinear DFT without Hubbard U and spin-orbit coupling often fails to capture the necessary exchange splitting.
The approach is most applicable when exchange interactions and spin-orbit effects are significant.
Strongly correlated systems may require refinement beyond the proposed approach.
Predicted energy differences and magnetic-moment magnitudes depend on the Hubbard U value and implementation details.
Total energies and computed magnetic moments can be used as observables when comparing magnetic configurations.
The hypothesis is falsified if adding Hubbard U and spin-orbit coupling does not produce a lower-energy ferromagnetic state or the expected non-zero moments relative to the baseline.
